item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 6
item.description: Oil held a two-day drop, as rising Persian Gulf exports and a steep price cut by Saudi Arabia reinforced signs of a loosening market.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: GPU Financing Filters Into ABS With Stonebriar, Wingspire Deals
item.description: The growing demand for capital to fund artificial intelligence investment is filtering into a little-watched corner of the asset-backed securities market: bonds secured by equipment loans and leases.
item.dc:creator: Menghan Xiao and Charles Williams

item.title: Mark Walter Charity’s CLO Tie-Up Maps Intricacies of His Empire
item.description: Even at the time, it was considered an unconventional alliance: Mark Walter committing $160 million through his education-focused nonprofit to help a Chicago credit investment firm comply with Dodd-Frank regulations in return for funding.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Graf and Miranda Davis

item.title: Babylist CEO on New NYC Showroom, Growth Targets
item.description: Babylist CEO Jennifer Hyman discusses the company’s new 20,000-square-foot showroom in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, which opened at the end of September and is its largest retail location yet. Hyman says the space is designed to help expecting and new parents research major purchases with expert guidance: visitors can learn about products, try baby carriers and get help installing car seats. She speaks with Scarlet Fu on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ellison's Skydance Announced Merger Details
item.description: Paramount Skydance Corp. outlined the executive leadership team that will helm the new company resulting from its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. David Ellison will continue to serve as chief executive officer and chairman, overseeing the company’s long-term strategy and creative vision, while co-CEO Ynon Kreiz will focus on day-to-day management. Bloomberg New Media Reporter Hannah Miller breaks down the latest news on the closely-watched merger. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: S&P 500 Closes In on Record High as Tech Rallies
item.description:
A rally in giant technology companies drove stocks higher in the Monday session, overshadowing concerns about still-elevated oil prices and bond yields.
The S&P 500 rose to a striking distance of a record while the Nasdaq 100 reached a fresh peak. Political upheaval in Europe and fiscal worries drove the euro to its weakest since May 2025, while longer-dated Treasury yields hit multi-decade highs. Markets have absorbed rising rates, high energy costs and renewed inflation concerns, with stocks continuing to advance.
For a look at the broader market backdrop, we hear from Carol Schleif, Chief Market Strategist at BMO Wealth Management. She speaks with Bloomberg Businessweek Daily hosts Carol Massar and Norah Mulinda. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: World’s Biggest Business Class Coming to British Airways’ A380s
item.description: British Airways will introduce what it called the world’s biggest business class on its upgraded double-decker Airbus SE A380 jets, targeting premium passengers as airlines rush to cash in on upscale travel.
item.dc:creator: Kate Duffy and Siddharth Philip

item.title: Could High US Bond Yields Spark A Crisis in Europe?
item.description: Bond yields are rising from the US to Japan — but the pressure is especially acute in France. How central banks could respond. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: PTC Rises on Schneider Electric’s $23.7 Billion Takeover Deal | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Scarlet Fu, Hema Parmar, Carol Massar and Norah Mulinda. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JPMorgan Dangles 11% Yield on Volta’s $5 Billion AI Loan Sale
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is pitching a yield of about 11% on a $5 billion leveraged-loan sale on behalf of Volta Infrastructure Holdings Ltd., one of the highest borrowing costs seen in the market for risky debt that’s become popular for financing the AI boom.
item.dc:creator: Paula Seligson and Gowri Gurumurthy

item.title: LA Schools Face High Fiscal Solvency Risk, State Report Finds
item.description: The Los Angeles Unified School District has a high fiscal solvency risk level as its yearslong enrollment decline continues, according to a new analysis from California officials.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Oxford

item.title: Corgi's 'Spaghetti Cannon,' New 10,000 S&P ETF
item.description: "Bloomberg ETF IQ" focuses on the opportunities, risks and current trends tied to the trillions of dollars in the global exchange traded funds industry. Today's guests: Invesco Global Head of ETFs & Index Strategies Brian Hartigan, TMX VettaFi Investment Strategist Cinthia Murphy, Corgi Chief Investment Strategist Jeff Weniger, and Roundhill Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sarah Jessica Parker, Astrea London Bet Big on Lab Grown Gemstones
item.description: Actress and global creative director of Astrea London Sarah Jessica Parker said that she was drawn to the lab grown jewelry company because of the combination of creativity and technology involved in the brand and that she found it exciting to try to 'be worthy' of carving out a new form of luxury in the lab grown diamond business. Parker, who was joined by Astrea London founder Nathalie Morrison, also discussed the future of the industry, which Morrison called 'a different era in luxury' focused on sustainability, craftsmanship, beauty and design. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Copper Advances as Tech Rally Outweighs Surging Bond Yields
item.description: Copper gained alongside US stocks as a rally in technology companies outweighed surging bond yields and concerns over Europe’s deepening fiscal strains.
item.dc:creator: Eddie Spence and James Attwood

item.title: Brazilian Real Outperforms on Elections, Leads LatAm FX Rally
item.description: Latin American currencies posted some of the biggest gains on Monday, with the Brazilian real spearheading the advance after right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro surged to a surprise lead in the first round of the presidential election.
item.dc:creator: Ray Ndlovu, Bhaskar Dutta and Nicolle Yapur

item.title: Brazil Assets Surge as Investor Favorite Bolsonaro Leads in Race
item.description: Brazilian assets surged on expectations that Flávio Bolsonaro will address the country’s mounting fiscal problems and pave the way for interest-rate cuts after he became the surprise favorite to win the presidency in an Oct. 25 runoff against Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo, Barbara Nascimento and Leda Alvim

item.title: Gold Steadies as Dollar Strengthens on European Debt Risks
item.description: Gold steadied after paring earlier gains Monday, pressured by a stronger dollar as European political uncertainty boosted the greenback’s appeal and traders weighed the outlook for interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Preeti Soni, Mark Burton and Sybilla Gross

item.title: S&P 500 Closes In on Record High as Tech Rallies: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to open higher after a tech-led rally pushed the S&P 500 index near a record as investors largely shrugged off concerns about bond yields at multi-decade highs. US oil prices extended declines.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Kutty Abraham

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 5
item.description: Oil fell as Saudi Arabia cut crude prices for Asian buyers in a sign that physical supplies are becoming more readily available as Middle Eastern exports recover.
item.dc:creator: Mia Gindis, Kanoko Matsuyama and Paul Burkhardt

item.title: Why Philosophers Are Worried About AI
item.description: Debate over artificial intelligence has largely focused on whether machines could become too powerful. Harvard philosopher Michael Sandel argues that a more immediate question is whether AI changes humans themselves: weakening authentic connection, independent thought and the ways people understand meaning and purpose. Universities are already confronting that challenge as students increasingly use AI to learn and communicate, while Vanderbilt University Chancellor Daniel Diermeier argues that technological fluency must be paired with the ability to think independently. University of Notre Dame philosophy professor Meghan Sullivan takes that question beyond the classroom, examining the ethical responsibility of the companies building AI and the role individuals have in deciding how the technology enters their everyday lives. (Source: Bloomberg)
